children: Rozebud Gonsalves Mumbai: Indian corporates are taking advantage of the prevailing surplus liquidity conditions and are continuing to tap the bond market despite higher yields and an uncertain rate outlook, corporate bond experts said. Several large issuers have raised funds in recent days, while more are expected to come to the market next week, ahead of a potential rate hike and expectations of tighter liquidity conditions.

The six-member Monetary Policy Committee will meet from October 5 to October 7 amid expectation of a 25 basis point hike in policy rate to 5.50%. Edelweiss Financial Services is set to raise 300 crore through a public NCD issue on Monday, while Bajaj Auto Credit and IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company are likely to raise 250 crores and 200 crores respectively.

Indian corporates are expected to raise over 1000 crores next week. Separately, Vedanta's board approved a 3,500-crore bond issuance and state owned Power Grid Corporation's board also approved a 5000 crore bond issue, according to a BSE. "I do not expect the corporate bond market to slow materially despite the increasing probability of higher interest rates.

In fact, there is a visible change in issuer behaviour. Several large issuers have been active and they are increasingly looking to lock in funding before system liquidity drains out and borrowing costs move higher," said Venkatakrishnan Srinivasan, managing partner at Rockfort Fincap, a debt advisory firm. Banking system liquidity has stood at a large surplus this month because of inflows from the FCNR(B) scheme. The daily average surplus this month was at 9.97 lakh crore, while in August it was 3.67 lakh crore and 1.07 in July, RBI data showed. The sharp increase in surplus liquidity has left banks looking for avenues to deploy these funds, and corporate bond issuances are emerging as one such avenue, experts said.

title: Corporates Crowd the Bond Market Amid Rate-Hike Buzz
